title: FACET: Teacher-Centred LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems—Towards Personalized Educational Worksheets
extended_summary:
This paper addresses the challenge of supporting differentiated instruction in heterogeneous mathematics classrooms. The authors argue that existing AI personalization tools are often performance-focused, student-facing, and insufficiently attentive to motivational and pedagogical factors that teachers must manage when creating instructional materials for diverse learners.

To address this problem, the paper introduces FACET, a teacher-centered, large language model-based multi-agent framework for generating individualized worksheets. FACET uses three specialized agents: learner agents that simulate student profiles, a teacher agent that creates didactically structured worksheets aligned with Bloom’s taxonomy, and an evaluator agent that provides quality feedback. The system is built to personalize tasks using both cognitive factors such as mathematical proficiency and motivational factors such as intrinsic motivation.

The framework is tested with authentic grade 8 mathematics curriculum content from German secondary education. Evaluation combines automated agent-based scoring across multiple worksheet iterations and exploratory feedback from five K-12 in-service teachers. The results suggest that the system produces stable, high-quality, and learner-aligned worksheets, with especially strong ratings for task suitability and clarity. Teacher feedback was broadly positive and emphasized the usefulness of adjustable difficulty, scaffolding, and motivational tailoring.

The authors conclude that multi-agent LLM architectures can feasibly support scalable teacher-facing personalization in mathematics education, but they also note that the current study is preliminary. They call for richer learner profiles, stronger curricular integration, and future in-classroom validation with real learners.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a peer-reviewed feasibility and qualitative evaluation, not an experimental study of learning outcomes. It uses internal agent-based ratings and exploratory teacher feedback, so it provides some empirical evidence but with limited causal credibility and external validity.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper shows promising but indirect benefits, mainly on worksheet quality and perceived suitability rather than student achievement. Because there is no measured effect on learning gains and no effect size, the practical impact on K-12 outcomes remains unclear.

interventions.use_case: teacher-facing LLM-based multi-agent system that simulates learner profiles and generates personalized mathematics worksheets with scaffolding, hints, motivational comments, and didactical sequencing for grade 8 classrooms

finding.finding_summary: The paper reports that FACET generated personalized grade 8 mathematics worksheets aligned to learner profiles, with high evaluator ratings for suitability and clarity. Across 10 internal evaluations per worksheet, suitability was very high (M=4.78, SD=0.06) and clarity was also high (M=4.76, SD=0.12) on a 1–6 inverted scale, suggesting the system can produce math tasks matched to cognitive level and motivation. However, this is a feasibility/quality study rather than a direct achievement test, so no learning gains were measured.
finding.measure: Automated evaluator ratings and teacher ratings of worksheet quality/suitability for grade 8 mathematics tasks
finding.study_size: n=4 learner profiles x 10 internal evaluations; n=5 teachers

finding.finding_summary: The system explicitly models intrinsic motivation alongside mathematical proficiency, and teacher feedback indicated that motivational tailoring was valuable, especially for low-motivation learners. Teachers suggested that narrative framing and everyday-life relevance could further improve engagement, implying the generated worksheets already supported motivation to some extent. No direct student motivation outcome was experimentally measured; evidence is based on expert judgments of motivational fit.
finding.measure: Teacher expert ratings and qualitative think-aloud feedback on motivational suitability

finding.finding_summary: The framework is presented as a teacher-facing tool intended to reduce prompting overhead and support scalable differentiation, and teachers described it as useful for adjusting tasks without moving students to other topics. While the paper does not quantify workload reduction, the qualitative feedback indicates potential efficiency gains in preparing differentiated worksheets for heterogeneous classrooms.
finding.measure: Teacher feedback on usability and preparation burden reduction
